tag: EP.12A · The Empty Line in the Ledger
title: The Empty Line in the Ledger

beats.t: Evening came for the first time to the island whose sun had returned. The sun descended toward the horizon on schedule. Occasional pot-lid beats still drifted from the square.
The seaside hill was quiet. Each time the waves licked the sand and withdrew, the smell of wet salt rose.
The black tiger lay on a rock. A thick ledger was open between its forepaws.
The paper was old, but the writing gleamed as though new. Every loan and collection recorded, not one line out of place.
Let's settle things. Start with today's receipts.
A claw turned the first page. The rustle cut clearly between the sounds of waves.
Underground stage. Twelve bundles of applause lent. Collection complete.
Singer Yeoul. One strand of voice. Collection complete.
If you stood onstage with borrowed applause, you repay it when you leave. Nobody forced anyone to borrow.
A silver thread unwound by itself between the ledger pages. It trembled finely, though there was no wind.
A tiny sound came from its tip. Someone drawing breath and choosing a first note.
Shh. You're mine. The price was paid.
The tiger pinned the thread with a claw and tucked it between the pages. It took a long time for the trembling to stop.
Then the sun on the horizon flickered once.
Where the light went out, the waves rose backward. Black finger marks approached across the sand, one by one.
Several black hands rose above the water. They encircled the tiger and opened their palms upward.
The sun has returned.
...It has. Because of the song.
A song. That pig's song.
I lost a feather. That child was a useful vessel.
The crow wasn't my assignment. I was only responsible for applause.
Then did you collect the applause?
The tiger's whiskers moved slightly. Its paw pressed harder against the ledger.
...Most of it.
The gold ring on its right forepaw heated. It narrowed a notch, biting into fur.
Ghh...!
Most. I never entrusted you with most.
The tiger lowered its head. As it steadied its breathing, fine heat kept spreading beneath the ring.
Next time, I will leave nothing.
You are a beast that keeps promises. That is why I chose you. Do not forget why you are here.
I have never forgotten. To stop that child before they become a monster.
The next island trades in time. Collect the pig's time there.
Leave not one hour. Only what is empty can be filled.
Filled? With what—
Instead of answering, the hands sank. Sunset spread again. As though nothing had happened, waves licked the sand.
The ring's heat did not fade easily. The tiger dipped its paw in seawater and withdrew it only much later.
Empty to be filled. Filled with what?
Doesn't matter. Collect what I'm told and it's over. That's the contract.
The tiger turned pages again. The final page for the Island of Expression held a line for the flower pig.
Nothing received. A thousand refused claps. One refused deal. Red writing appeared beside them of its own accord.
[ Flower Pig · Uncollected ]
Uncollected...?
The tiger rubbed the letters with a paw. The red writing neither smeared nor vanished.
My ledger has no uncollected entries. Never has.
I said refusal had its own price. So collect it. Simple arithmetic.
Despite those words, the claw lingered over the line.
The daytime scene kept overlapping it. A pink pig standing voiceless onstage, holding up a pot lid.
Idiot. Borrowed applause would have been so much easier.
Stops at every injury. Gives freely. Refuses what's offered. Someone like that won't last.
...And someone like that becomes a monster? The numbers don't add up.
Then rain sounded from the sea. The tiger lifted its head. The sky was clear, only the sunset red.
The rain was sounding only inside its ears.
A brief scene flashed. Wet asphalt. A flickering bus-stop light. A yellow umbrella tilted overhead.
Someone smiled beneath the umbrella. No face visible. Only a half-soaked shoulder.
...What was that?
The rain cut off. Only waves remained. The tiger pressed a paw to its forehead.
I'm tired. I policed an entire island.
The tiger turned back several pages. The Island of Companions. One line still needed erasing there.
[ Drumming child · Name — Held in safekeeping ]
One name. Change safekeeping to collection complete, and it's done.
The tiger felt inside its cloak. In a small pocket stitched with gold thread, one name pulsed warmly.
One stroke of a claw would transfer the child's name into the ledger. The tiger looked down at the scar that would remain on the wrist. Once handed over, a name was not easily returned.
The claw did not fall. The tiger pushed the pocket deeper into the cloak.
Later. After the next island.
The child's drumming in the square still echoed in its ears. A beat that never faltered, played by someone who did not even know his own name.
Last, the tiger took the gray feather from its cloak. The feather the crow had left behind.
Its tip was still warm. Bringing an ear close, the tiger heard the faintest humming.
Wanted to sing together, did you.
Everyone says that at first. One bout of ridicule, and it's over.
It was for me too.
The tiger shut its mouth, startled by its own words. It could not remember what it meant.
It did not enter the feather in the ledger. Instead, it tucked it into the innermost part of the cloak, beside Captain Drum's name.
The gold ring tightened again. The tiger gritted its teeth and closed the book.
The next island. Where they sell time. Every last moment of that pig's time.
Debts grow when you leave them. So this time, nothing uncollected.
The tiger descended the hill. Footprints trailed across wet sand, then ended at the water.
Wind lifted one corner of the ledger. Inside the closed book, the two red characters still refused to go dark.
The tiger's body dissolved into black mist and scattered over the sea. Beyond the horizon, toward the island of ticking clocks.
